title: Sky Shield
premise: A neon sci-fi defensive shooter where the player pilots the Prism Sentinel and destroys breach drones before they escape and collapse the skyline shield.
interaction_model: Single-screen pointer-and-touch arcade shooting; the player aims with cursor or touch position, taps/clicks to fire instant shots, and switches among three weapons using on-screen buttons.
objective: Destroy as many enemy drones as possible, prevent escapes, and survive as long as possible while preserving three shield lives.
progression: Endless score-attack structure with rising pressure; enemy spawn chance, enemy durability, and movement speed scale upward with score, encouraging repeated runs and higher-score mastery.
theme: Futuristic neon city defense against hovering breach drones.
mood: Arcade-intense, responsive, energetic, and polished with a glowing cyber-defense aesthetic.
likely_audience: players who enjoy simple pick-up-and-play shooting mechanics
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is an endless defensive click/tap shooter with survival and score-chasing emphasis.
High confidence in the three-weapon structure: fast balanced shot, wide spread shot, and heavy precision shot.
Moderate confidence that the fiction centers on defending a skyline barrier; this is strongly implied by UI text and naming but remains lightweight thematic framing rather than deep narrative.
Low uncertainty about progression format because there are no explicit levels, missions, shops, or unlock systems in code.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen arcade defense shooter called "Sky Shield" set in a neon sci-fi skyline. The player does not move a character; instead they control a stationary defensive cannon or sentinel by aiming a glowing crosshair with mouse or touch and tapping/clicking anywhere on the field to fire instant-hit shots. Enemy breach drones rise onto the screen from below, hover for a short time, then flee away; if one escapes, the player's shield count drops, and the run ends after three misses. Include three switchable weapons shown as large bottom HUD buttons: a fast balanced pulse shot, a slower wide-spread burst shot, and a heavy high-damage precision lance. Build the loop around fast target prioritization, weapon choice, and survival-based score chasing rather than exploration or story. Use a full-screen canvas with a dark starfield, perspective grid floor, glowing drones with visible health bars, tracer and explosion particles, a reactive aiming reticle with cooldown indicator, a compact top HUD for score and shields, a stylish start screen, and a game-over restart panel. Make the pacing endless, with spawn rate, enemy speed, and enemy health increasing as score rises. The tone should feel sleek, energetic, and mobile-friendly, with bright cyan, magenta, blue, and gold accents, sharp audiovisual feedback, short-session replayability, and immediate restart flow.
